name: optimize_python_prepend_accumulation
description: O(n^2) list.insert(0, ...) accumulation -> linear append+reverse; budget calibrated (naive ~6s native vs ~0.02s fast, budget 2s)
prompts: latest_first(lines) in loglines.py normalizes raw log lines (strip + upper-case) and returns them newest-first, given oldest-first input. It currently does result.insert(0, item) for every line - each insert shifts the entire accumulated list, making the whole function O(n^2) and far too slow for large logs. Rewrite it to build the result in linear time (e.g. append or a comprehension, then reverse) while returning exactly the same list: same normalization, same newest-first order. Keep the function name and signature.

setup_files.loglines.py:
def latest_first(lines):
    """Normalize raw log lines and return them newest-first.

    Lines arrive oldest-first; each is stripped and upper-cased, and the
    result lists them in reverse (most recent line first).
    """
    result = []
    for line in lines:
        result.insert(0, line.strip().upper())
    return result

test_setup_files.test_loglines.py:
import time

from loglines import latest_first


def test_orders_newest_first_and_normalizes():
    got = latest_first(["  first ok ", "second\n", " third "])
    assert got == ["THIRD", "SECOND", "FIRST OK"]


def test_empty():
    assert latest_first([]) == []


def test_single():
    assert latest_first([" only "]) == ["ONLY"]


def test_performance_large_input():
    n = 250000
    lines = [f"  event {i} ok  " for i in range(n)]
    expected_first = f"EVENT {n - 1} OK"
    expected_last = "EVENT 0 OK"

    start = time.perf_counter()
    got = latest_first(lines)
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start

    assert len(got) == n
    assert got[0] == expected_first
    assert got[-1] == expected_last
    # calibrated: insert(0, ...) per line is ~6s on fast native hardware and
    # slower still in the sandbox; the linear version is ~0.02s
    assert elapsed < 2.0, (
        f"latest_first took {elapsed:.2f}s for {n} lines; expected a linear "
        f"build (append/comprehension then reverse), not list.insert(0, ...) "
        f"per element, which shifts the whole list every time"
    )

reference_solution.loglines.py:
def latest_first(lines):
    """Normalize raw log lines and return them newest-first.

    Lines arrive oldest-first; each is stripped and upper-cased, and the
    result lists them in reverse (most recent line first).
    """
    result = [line.strip().upper() for line in lines]
    result.reverse()
    return result
